A rollout takes one release to every system in rings: a practice run on a throwaway copy first, then the blank system new customers are made from, then one customer on their own with a day of watching, then everybody. Each real customer is updated inside their own quiet window, and the whole thing stops at the first thing that goes wrong.

Exactly this, in exactly this order, and it stops at the first thing that goes wrong. Nothing here has happened yet.
Left out, and why
The practice run happens as soon as you press the button and takes a minute or two, so you see whether the update works before anybody else does. Everything after it waits for its own window.
Leave behind
They stay on the old release. The rollout carries on to everybody else. Somebody has to bring them in step on their own later.
Call this rollout off

Every system that has not been updated yet is left on the old release. What has already gone out stays out. This is also the right thing to do with one that is stopped and not going to continue — a rollout left lying about holds the one practice copy everybody else needs.
